title: The Car Stunt's Utmost Limit
notes: Detective-cast (Conan, the Detective Boys incl. Genta -- whose souvenir sticker becomes a physical clue, and Professor Agasa; also Inspector Megure/Takagi) omitted as person nodes by convention, matching the old case file. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. Murderer identity (Fukamachi) matches the old case file's s1 -- no culprit discrepancy here. However the old file's clue c1 ('a coat fragment caught in the crashed car's door but absent from earlier footage') has the finding backwards: the transcript's actual clue is that Rikiishi's cape/cloak is NOT caught in the door and the door is never seen opening/closing during the ramp-up footage, which (combined with the crashed car's engine still being hot immediately after impact, proving it had just been actively driven rather than idle since the ramp climb) is what proves a car swap happened on the roof out of camera view. The old file's c2 ('remote control found on his person') overstates what's shown -- the transcript only establishes Fukamachi borrowed the remote from Nishiwaki under the pretense of wanting to inspect it and it surfaces again at the reveal, not that it was found on his body. Also added: the duplicate Kamen-Yaiba-sticker clue (Genta stickered both cars identically), which the old file omitted entirely and which is actually what makes the sticker-based car ID a false lead in-episode. Speaker attribution in the multi-way argument scene (~13:48-14:20) about who hit whom over what is not tagged by speaker in the subtitle track; assignments below (Kijima punched over reporting Rikiishi to producers, Nakasato punched over shoddy maintenance, Nishiwaki slapped repeatedly and threatened Rikiishi at drinking parties) follow the most consistent reading of the back-and-forth accusations. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The crashed car's hood was still hot right after impact, though the car assumed to be idle Car A should have cooled since the ramp drive -- proves the crashed car had just been actively driven, i.e. it was really Car B.
Ramp-up footage shows Rikiishi's cape never caught in the door and the door never opens or closes -- rules out a car swap happening on camera, pointing instead to a swap on the roof out of view.
Both Car A and Car B carry identical Kamen Yaiba stickers, so the sticker seen on the car left on the roof cannot actually prove that car is Car B.
